## Welcome back, divers {.section-break}

**Chapter 1 — Getting Started with Data in R**

Slides are a *scaffold*: one idea per slide, frequent retrieval check-ins, predict-then-check prompts. Click through and pause where you like.

## What you'll be able to do

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

- Distinguish between R (the language) and RStudio (the environment for using it)
- Install and load R packages from CRAN
- Explore a data frame using functions like `glimpse()` and `View()`
- Identify whether a variable is *categorical* or *quantitative*

::: {.predict}
Before we begin: which of these objectives feels least familiar to you right now? Hold that in mind — we'll check back at the end.
:::

## Check-in: What are R and RStudio?

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q1. What is the difference between R and RStudio?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>R is a web browser; RStudio is a desktop application</li>
  <li>R is the programming language; RStudio is an integrated development environment (IDE) for using R</li>
  <li>R is a graphical interface; RStudio is a command-line tool</li>
  <li>They are two different names for the same software</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> R is the programming language and engine that runs your code. RStudio is an IDE — a friendlier interface for writing R code, viewing data, and managing projects. The chapter's analogy: R is the engine, RStudio is the dashboard.</div>
:::

## Check-in: How do I code in R?

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q2. A column of phone numbers stored as text like `&quot;(555) 123-4567&quot;`. This variable is best classified as:</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Numerical, because it contains digits</li>
  <li>Categorical, because phone numbers identify entities rather than measure a quantity</li>
  <li>Numerical, because you could perform calculations on the digits</li>
  <li>Both numerical and categorical</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> The test for &quot;numerical&quot; is whether *arithmetic on the values is meaningful*, not whether digits appear. Adding two phone numbers makes no sense — they're identifiers, so they're categorical. Same logic applies to ZIP codes, customer IDs, and area codes.</div>
:::

## What are R packages? &mdash; live code

::: {.try-this}
Open RStudio (or paste into the book's webR block) and run the canonical example for this section. Ask one student to predict the output **before** running.
:::

```r
# Replace with the section's canonical code chunk.

library(tidyverse)

# e.g.,

```

## Check-in: What are R packages?

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="b"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q3. After running `install.packages(&quot;dplyr&quot;)` once, you close R and reopen it the next day. To use `glimpse()` again, you need to:</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>Re-install the package</li>
  <li>Run `library(dplyr)` again — the install persists, but the loading does not</li>
  <li>Nothing — packages stay loaded forever once installed</li>
  <li>Type `glimpse()` and R will auto-load the package</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(b)</strong> Installation is a one-time act per machine. *Loading* with `library(pkg)` happens at the start of every new R session — that's why scripts begin with `library()` calls.</div>
:::

## Check-in: Explore your first datasets

::: {.predict}
Take 30 seconds. Predict your answer **before** clicking. Then tap your choice.
:::

::: {.mcq data-correct="c"}
<div class="mcq-stem">Q4. Which of these object names is **invalid** in R?</div>
<ol class="mcq-options">
  <li>`flight_data`</li>
  <li>`flightData`</li>
  <li>`2021_flights`</li>
  <li>`flights2021`</li>
</ol>
<div class="mcq-controls">
<button class="poll-btn show-poll">Show class poll</button>
<button class="show-answer">Show answer</button>
</div>
<div class="poll-bar"></div>
<div class="mcq-reveal"><strong>(c)</strong> R object names cannot start with a digit. `2021_flights` errors; `flights2021` (digit not first) is fine. They also cannot start with `_` or contain spaces.</div>
:::
